You now have OgreBot installed and running. Here is where to go from here:

  • First Run Guide -- Learn the basics of the OgreBot UI and essential settings
  • FAQ -- Common questions and troubleshooting
  • Profiles -- Understanding how to save and share your configuration
  • Aliases -- Set up group member references

Sample Profiles

Every class comes with a sample profile that gives you a working starting point. You can start playing immediately and fine-tune settings as you learn the system.

docs.title: Removing Memory and FPS Display
docs.text: By default, InnerSpace shows memory usage and FPS counters in the top-left corner of your screen. These are InnerSpace features, not ISXOgre features. Here is how to hide them.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Right-click the InnerSpace icon in your system tray and select Configuration
  2. Under Session (not Uplink), click Startup (not Pre-Startup)
  3. Select the entry you want to hide -- either Memory Indicator or FPS Indicator
  4. Change -show to -hide
  5. Click Apply, then Accept
  6. Close all EQ2 sessions and restart InnerSpace for the change to take effect

Keep the Entry

Changing -show to -hide is better than deleting the entry entirely. This way you can easily re-enable the display later by changing it back to -show.

docs.title: Repatching ISXOgre
docs.text: ISXOgre uses OgrePatcher to keep all files up to date. The patcher automatically scans every file it needs each time you load ISXOgre.

docs.title: Automatic Patching
docs.text: Simply opening a new EQ2 session and loading ISXOgre will automatically check for and apply any needed patches. In most cases, you do not need to do anything special.

docs.title: Manual Repatch
docs.text:
If you are already in-game and need to force a repatch without restarting:

  1. Open the InnerSpace console (press ~)
  2. Type the following command and press Enter:
ext -unload isxogre && timedcommand 10 ext isxogre

This unloads ISXOgre and reloads it, which triggers the patcher to rescan all files.

docs.title: Why OgreBot?
docs.text: OgreBot is a UI-driven, fully customizable adventure bot for EverQuest 2. Whether you are boxing a full group or just want a helping hand on your main character, OgreBot handles combat, buffing, healing, and much more -- all without requiring you to write a single line of code.

docs.title: Full UI Control
docs.text:
OgreBot gives you control over nearly every aspect of the bot through an intuitive, in-game user interface. You do not need to edit config files, write scripts, or learn a programming language. Everything from ability priorities to healing thresholds can be configured by clicking checkboxes, adjusting sliders, and reordering lists.

No Coding Required

Unlike many automation tools, OgreBot is designed so that you never need to look at a piece of code to get up and running.

docs.title: Automatic Spell Management
docs.text: One of OgreBot's standout features is its automated spell export system. You run the export once per character, and OgreBot learns all of your abilities, AAs, and spells. When new spells are added, a level cap increases, or new AA lines are introduced, your new abilities are automatically imported the next time you export -- no manual spell list editing required.

docs.title: Frequent Updates
docs.text: OgreBot is actively maintained. Updates generally come on a weekly basis, and bug fixes are typically released within 24 hours of being discovered. When you launch ISXOgre, files are automatically updated so you are always running the latest version.

docs.title: Works Across All Classes
docs.text: OgreBot does not use separate class files. Most abilities work universally across all classes, with class-specific options appearing only when relevant. This means less setup and fewer things that can break when game changes happen.

docs.title: Crowd Control Built In
docs.text: OgreBot includes full mezzing (crowd control) support out of the box. Enchanters and other CC-capable classes can automatically manage adds without any extra configuration beyond enabling the feature.

docs.title: Quick Setup
docs.text: OgreBot is designed to be a plug-and-play experience. After installation, you can be up and running within minutes. Every class ships with a sample profile that gives you a working starting point, so you can jump into gameplay immediately and fine-tune settings as you learn.

docs.title: Active Community
docs.text: OgreBot has an active community on Discord, IRC, and the forums. Other users are happy to share profiles, tips, and encounter strategies. You are never on your own when trying to figure something out.

docs.title: What Can OgreBot Do?
docs.text:
Here is a quick overview of the major features included with your subscription:

Feature Description Combat Automation Manages your cast stack, ability rotations, and combat arts Healing and Curing Automatic healing, curing, and resurrection Buffing Maintains buffs on yourself and group members Crowd Control Automatic mezzing and CC management Assist and Targeting Configurable assist targets and auto-targeting Following Automatic follow with customizable distance Looting Configurable loot handling and distribution Instance Controller Automated boss fight mechanics for supported zones Profile System Save, load, and share configurations across characters OgreCraft Full crafting automation (included with subscription) Harvesting Automated resource gathering Inventory Management Bag sorting, item management, and more

All Included

OgreBot and OgreCraft are bundled together in a single subscription. You get access to all tools and features, plus all future updates.

docs.title: Ready to Get Started?
docs.text: Head over to the Installation Guide to set everything up, or check the FAQ if you have questions.

docs.title: OgreBot
docs.text: OgreBot is the core automation tool for EverQuest 2, providing intelligent combat automation, group coordination, and extensive customization through its tabbed interface.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Intelligent Combat - Automated ability casting with customizable priority and cast stacks
  • Group Coordination - Cross-session commands to control your entire group from one character
  • Profile System - Save and share configurations per class and character
  • Instance Controller - Automated instance running with fight-specific mechanics handling
  • Extensible - Full scripting API for developers to create custom behaviors

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: OgreBot's settings are organized into tabs. Each tab controls a different aspect of the bot's behavior. Start with the Settings and Setup tabs to configure the basics.

docs.title: Targeting
docs.text: OgreBot uses an alias system to reference characters by role instead of name. For example, @Tank always refers to your group's tank regardless of who's playing.

docs.title: Communication
docs.text: You can use cross-session commands to control your characters.

docs.title: Saving Settings
docs.text: The profile system lets you save your entire configuration and share it between characters of the same class.

docs.title: Aliases
docs.text: An alias is a way to identify a character by role instead of by name. Instead of updating every setting when your group composition changes, you can use aliases like @Tank or *Healer and OgreBot resolves them to the right character automatically.

docs.title: Quick Links
docs.text:
• Alias Types — Built-in, user-defined, pet, and direct names
  • Built-in Alias Reference — Full list of @ aliases
  • Using Aliases — Where and how to use them
  • Colour Codes — What the colours mean on the Aliases tab
  • Viewing Active Aliases — How to display current aliases

docs.title: Alias Types
docs.text: OgreBot supports three types of aliases:

docs.title: Built-in Aliases (@ prefix)
docs.text: These are determined automatically by OgreBot based on your current group composition. You cannot modify them -- they update dynamically as group members change.

docs.title: User-Defined Aliases (* prefix)
docs.text: These are aliases you create yourself on the Aliases tab. Use these when you want to assign a custom name to a specific group member or role that the built-in aliases do not cover.

docs.title: Pet Aliases (Pet: prefix)
docs.text: These reference the pet owned by a specific player. For example, Pet:Kannkor targets whatever pet Kannkor currently has active.

docs.title: Direct Names
docs.text: You can also use a player's character name directly without any prefix. This references that player as a group or raid member.

docs.title: Built-in Alias Reference
docs.text: Alias Targets @Me Your current character @Group Each group member individually @Raid The entire raid roster @NotSelfGroup All group members except yourself @PCTarget The player character you currently have targeted @Tank The fighter in your group @Bard The bard in your group @Enchanter The enchanter in your group @Healer1 through @Healer6 Healers by priority @DPS1 through @DPS6 DPS characters by priority

docs.title: Healer Priority Order
docs.text:
When multiple healers are in the group, they are assigned in this order:

  1. Shaman (Mystic, Defiler)
  2. Druid (Fury, Warden)
  3. Cleric (Templar, Inquisitor)
  4. Shaper (Channeler)

So @Healer1 is always the Shaman (if one exists), @Healer2 is the Druid, and so on.

docs.title: DPS Priority Order
docs.text:
When multiple DPS are in the group, they are assigned in this order:

  1. Sorcerer (Wizard, Warlock)
  2. Predator (Ranger, Assassin)
  3. Animalist (Beastlord)
  4. Summoner (Conjuror, Necromancer)
  5. Rogue (Brigand, Swashbuckler)

Multiple of the Same Archetype

If you have two characters of the same archetype (e.g., two Sorcerers), they are randomly assigned between the numbered aliases. The ordering between same-archetype members is not guaranteed.

docs.title: Using Aliases
docs.text:
Aliases can be used anywhere OgreBot expects a character name:

  • Assist tab -- Set your assist target to @Tank
  • Cast Stack -- Target heals to @Healer1 or *MainTank
  • Chat Commands -- Reference group members by role

docs.title: Example: Setting Up a Custom Alias
docs.text:
1. Open the OgreBot main UI
  2. Click the Aliases tab
  3. Add a new entry with a * prefix name (e.g., *MT)
  4. Set its value to the character name of your main tank

Now you can use *MT anywhere in OgreBot and it resolves to that character.

docs.title: Colour Codes
docs.text:
The Aliases tab uses colour coding to show the status of each alias at a glance:

Colour In Cast Stack? Alias Matches Name? 🟢 Green Yes Yes 🟡 Yellow Yes No 🟠 Orange No Yes 🔴 Red No No
  • Green -- The alias is used in the cast stack, and the alias points to the correct character name
  • Yellow -- The alias is used in the cast stack, but the alias does NOT point to that character name
  • Orange -- The alias is NOT used in the cast stack, but the alias does point to that character name
  • Red -- The alias is NOT used in the cast stack, and the alias does NOT point to that character name

docs.title: Viewing Active Aliases
docs.text:
To see all currently active aliases and what they resolve to:

  1. Open the OgreBot UI
  2. Go to the Aliases tab
  3. Click the Display Aliases button

This prints all active aliases and their current targets to the InnerSpace console.

docs.title: Instance Controller
docs.text: The Instance Controller is OgreBot's system for automating boss fight mechanics in EverQuest 2 dungeons and raids. Instead of manually handling every mechanic (jousting, target switching, clicking objects, etc.), the Instance Controller runs specialized scripts that handle these mechanics for you.

docs.title: What Does It Do?
docs.text:
When you enter a supported zone, the Instance Controller can:

  • Joust automatically -- Move characters out of AoE range and back in at the right time
  • Switch targets -- Automatically target adds, specific NPCs, or objects during fight phases
  • Click objects -- Interact with zone objects during scripted events
  • Handle curses and detriments -- Respond to specific debuffs that require player action
  • Manage positioning -- Move characters to safe spots during dangerous mechanics
  • Coordinate the group -- Issue commands to all characters simultaneously

Zone Support

The Instance Controller only works in zones that have scripts written for them. Not every zone is supported, and new zone scripts are added over time as content is released.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. When you zone into a supported instance, OgreBot detects the zone
  2. If an Instance Controller script exists for that zone, it loads automatically
  3. The script monitors the fight and triggers mechanics as needed
  4. You can also start instance scripts manually from the OgreBot UI

docs.title: Supported Zones
docs.text:
Instance Controller scripts are organized by expansion:

Expansion Folder Rage of Cthurath (current) _Exp_22_Rage_of_Cthurath Scars of Destruction _Exp_21_Scars_of_Destruction Ballads of Zimara _Exp_20_Ballads_of_Zimara

Each expansion folder contains scripts for both heroic instances and raid zones. The number of supported encounters varies per expansion.

docs.title: Automatic Mode
docs.text: In most cases, Instance Controller scripts load and run automatically when you enter a supported zone. No manual intervention is needed.

docs.title: Manual Control
docs.text:
If you need to start or restart an instance script:

  1. Open the OgreBot main UI
  2. Navigate to the Instance Controller section
  3. Select the zone and encounter
  4. Start the script

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
Group Leader

Instance Controller commands are typically issued by the group leader's session. Make sure OgreBot is running on your group leader character for full functionality.

Stay Updated

Instance Controller scripts are updated when encounter mechanics change. Keep ISXOgre up to date to ensure you have the latest scripts for current content.

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text: Profiles are how OgreBot saves and loads all of your settings. Every checkbox, ability priority, heal threshold, alias, and configuration option is stored in a profile. Understanding the profile system helps you manage settings efficiently across multiple characters.

docs.title: What Is a Profile?
docs.text:
A profile is an XML file stored in the EQ2OgreBot/Save/ folder. It contains everything about how OgreBot is configured for a character: the Settings tab, Cast Stack, Ability Rotation, Aliases, HUD positions, and every other tab in the UI.

When OgreBot starts, it loads a profile and applies all of its settings. When you make changes in the UI, those changes are saved back to the profile.

docs.title: Character-Specific Profiles
docs.text:
By default, each character gets its own profile file named after the server and character:

  • EQ2Save_Maj'Dul_MyWizard.xml
  • EQ2Save_Isle of Refuge_MyTank.xml

This means every character has completely independent settings.

docs.title: Master Profiles (Recommended)
docs.text:
A Master Profile is a single profile shared by all characters of the same class. Instead of maintaining separate profiles for each of your six Rangers, one Master profile handles all of them.

Example: EQ2Save_Master_Ranger.xml is used by every Ranger character on your account.

Why Use Master Profiles?

Master profiles save you significant time. When you update your Ranger's Cast Stack, the change applies to all your Rangers automatically. No need to update each character individually.

docs.title: How Master Profiles Are Assigned
docs.text:
OgreBot uses a routing file called EQ2Save_Settings.xml to decide which profile each character loads. The routing works by priority:

Priority Matches On Example 1 (highest) Server + Class + Character Maj'Dul.Wizard.MyWiz 2 Class + Character Wizard.MyWiz 3 Character name only MyWiz 4 Server + Class Maj'Dul.Wizard 5 Class only Wizard 6 Global fallback all 7 (lowest) Auto-generated Default filename pattern

The most common setup is to add an entry at priority 5 (class only), which makes all characters of that class use the same Master profile:

Wizard  -->  EQ2Save_Master_Wizard.xml
Ranger  -->  EQ2Save_Master_Ranger.xml

If you need one specific character to use different settings, add a higher-priority entry for just that character.

docs.title: Profile Parts
docs.text: Profile Parts let you split specific tabs out of your main profile into separate files. This is useful for sharing common settings across all characters regardless of class.

docs.title: Why Use Profile Parts?
docs.text:
Consider these tabs that are the same for every character you play:

  • Pack Pony -- inventory management (same for everyone)
  • HUDs -- HUD positions on your screen (same for all DPS, or same for all tanks)
  • Settings -- master checkboxes (similar for tanks vs. non-tanks)
  • Overseer -- overseer preferences (same for everyone)
  • OSA -- on-screen assistant (same for everyone)

Without Profile Parts, you would need to update each of these in every Master profile whenever you make a change. With Profile Parts, these shared tabs live in separate files and every profile references the same file.

docs.title: How Profile Parts Work
docs.text:
1. Profile Parts files are stored in EQ2OgreBot/Save/ProfileParts/
  2. Your main profile contains a mapping that says "for this tab, load from this external file"
  3. When Profile Parts are enabled, OgreBot loads each mapped tab from its external file instead of from the main profile
  4. Tabs without a mapping still load normally from the main profile

docs.title: Common Profile Parts Setup
docs.text:
Part File What It Contains Shared By Settings_Tank.xml Tank-specific checkbox settings All tank classes Settings_NotTank.xml DPS/Healer checkbox settings All non-tank classes HUD_Tank.xml Tank HUD positions All tank classes HUD_NotTank.xml DPS/Healer HUD positions All non-tank classes PackPony_AllToons.xml Pack pony configuration All characters OSA_AllToons.xml On-Screen Assistant settings All characters Overseer_AllToons.xml Overseer preferences All characters

Profile Parts Are Optional

You do not need to use Profile Parts to use OgreBot. They are an organizational tool for players who box many characters and want to keep shared settings in one place.

docs.title: Importing Profiles From Others
docs.text: One of the most common profile tasks is importing someone else's Cast Stack (ability priorities) into your own profile. Here is how to do it safely.

docs.title: What Is Safe to Import
docs.text:
These tabs are class-specific and are the most common things to import:

Tab Notes Cast Stack Ability priorities -- this is the main reason to import Ability Rotation Ability-specific durations and interrupt settings Item Rotation Item usage configuration Pre-Cast / Post-Cast Ability linking before/after casts

docs.title: What to Keep From Your Own Profile
docs.text:
These tabs contain personal settings that should not be overwritten:

Tab Why Keep Yours Settings Your personal enable/disable preferences Setup Your thresholds (attack %, heal %, follow distance) HUDs Your screen layout positions Aliases Your group member mappings Assist Your assist target Loot Your loot preferences Profile Parts Your Profile Parts configuration Load Execute Your custom scripts that run on profile load

docs.title: How to Merge a Profile
docs.text:
Always Back Up First

Before making any changes, copy your current profile to a backup file. If anything goes wrong, you can restore it.

The safe approach:

  1. Back up your current profile (e.g., copy EQ2Save_Master_Wizard.xml to EQ2Save_Master_Wizard_backup.xml)
  2. Open the other player's profile in a text editor
  3. Copy only the Cast Stack section (the <Set Name="CastStack">...</Set> block)
  4. Open your profile in a text editor
  5. Replace only the Cast Stack section in your profile with the copied one
  6. Save and reload OgreBot

Profile Parts Alternative

You can also save an imported Cast Stack as a Profile Part. Create a new file in the ProfileParts/ folder with just the Cast Stack data, and map it in your profile. This keeps your main profile clean and makes it easy to swap between different Cast Stacks.

docs.title: Loading Profiles
docs.text:
You can switch profiles without restarting OgreBot:

  • From the UI: Use the profile dropdown in the OgreBot interface
  • From the console: Type the appropriate load command
  • Cross-session: Load a profile on all characters at once using cross-session commands

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
How Profile Loading Works:

EQ2Save_Settings.xml  --->  EQ2Save_Master_Ranger.xml
    (routing table)              (main profile)
                                      |
                     +----------------+----------------+
                     |                |                |
               Tabs from main    Tabs from parts   Tabs from main
               (CastStack,      (Settings,         (Aliases,
                Setup, etc.)     HUDs, PackPony)    Assist, etc.)
                                      |
                               ProfileParts/
                               +-- Settings_NotTank.xml
                               +-- HUD_NotTank.xml
                               +-- PackPony_AllToons.xml
                               +-- OSA_AllToons.xml
                               +-- Overseer_AllToons.xml

Key takeaway: When importing a profile from someone else, only update the class-specific tabs (Cast Stack, Ability Rotation, etc.). Your personal settings and shared Profile Parts remain untouched.

docs.title: OgreBot Tabs Overview
docs.text: OgreBot's interface is organized into tabs, each controlling a different aspect of bot behavior. This page provides a quick reference to all available tabs.

docs.title: Core Tabs
docs.text: Tab Description Settings Main bot toggles - combat, healing, buffs, loot, resurrection Setup Initial character setup and configuration Settings 2 Additional settings and toggles Assist Assist target configuration and combat engagement Loot Loot rules, filters, and automation

docs.title: Casting Tabs
docs.text: Tab Description Cast Stack Ability priority ordering for combat Pre-Cast Abilities to cast before engaging combat Post-Cast Abilities to cast after combat ends Ascension Ascension ability configuration Ability Embargo Temporarily disable specific abilities

docs.title: Targeting & Control
docs.text: Tab Description Auto Target Automatic target selection rules Crowd Control Mez, stun, and crowd control management Items Item usage during combat (potions, poisons, etc.)

docs.title: Communication & Events
docs.text: Tab Description Announce Combat announcements and notifications Chat Events Respond to chat triggers Spawn Events React when NPCs spawn Despawn Events React when NPCs despawn On Zone Actions to perform when zoning

docs.title: Configuration & Management
docs.text: Tab Description Aliases Target aliases (@Tank, @Healer, etc.) OSA Ogre Script Automation Other Miscellaneous settings Relay Groups Communication group setup Load Load profiles and settings Unload Unload the bot

docs.title: Information & Debugging
docs.text: Tab Description Equipment Info View equipped gear details HUDs Heads-up display configuration OgreConsole In-game command console Uplink Info Connection and uplink status Key Binds Keyboard shortcut configuration EQ2 Chars Character information Debug Debugging tools and output Admin Administrative settings

docs.title: Ability Embargo
docs.text:
The Ability Embargo tab allows you to control abilities so they can be delayed for yourself or rotated within a raid. For instance, abilities like Glacial Freeze can be prevented from simultaneous casting across the group by setting embargo durations that prevent recasting within specified timeframes.

Important

Ability Embargo must be enabled in the Settings tab for these functions to operate.

docs.title: Frame 1: Full Ability List
docs.text: Displays all available abilities that can have embargo settings applied.

docs.title: Duration in seconds
docs.text: Specifies how long before an ability can be recast by another group or raid member.

docs.title: Add Duration / Subtract Duration
docs.text: Increases or decreases the embargo duration by a specified number of seconds.

docs.title: Checkboxes
docs.text: Checkbox Abbreviation Description Announce via IRC [IRC] Broadcasts embargo activity to IRC channels Group Members only will embargo [G] Restricts embargo listening to local group members only Only will embargo [Me] Applies embargo only to the current character Include caster and ability [I] Outputs ability and caster names instead of ID numbers Globally Mute messages -- Silences console messages while preserving IRC notifications

docs.title: Frame 3: Ability Embargo List
docs.text: Shows all currently active embargoes and their remaining durations.

docs.title: Admin
docs.text:
The Admin tab provides administrative functions for OgreBot profile management.

For profile parts documentation, see the OgreGaming Forums - Profile Parts.

Documentation coming soon.

docs.title: Announce
docs.text:
The Announce tab controls when the bot communicates with others using chat macros similar to player communication.

Warning

Exercise caution when using this feature with actual players. The bot may attempt to cast spells in situations beyond its control. For instance, if a target cannot be acquired, the bot lacks the ability to detect this limitation and will still attempt the spell cast.

docs.title: Target Replacement
docs.text:
The *Target* placeholder automatically substitutes the ability's target name. This placeholder can be used multiple times within the text.

Example: A message stating *Target* I am casting an ability on you *Target* directed at character Kannkor would announce: Kannkor I am casting an ability on you Kannkor

docs.title: Announce Target Settings
docs.text: You configure three elements for each announcement: the ability, the target, and the message text.

docs.title: Communication Methods
docs.text: Method Description Group Broadcasts via /gsay command Raid Broadcasts via /raid command Tell To Target Sends a private message to the ability's target using /tell

docs.title: Text Execution
docs.text: The Included in text option executes commands as written. For example, /gc blah blah *Target* becomes /gc blah blah Kannkor.

docs.title: NULL Fragment Restriction
docs.text: Messages containing "NULL" will not be announced, as the system interprets this as indicating an error. This limitation prevents announcing abilities or character names containing "null" (such as Warlock's Null Caress).

docs.title: Ascension
docs.text: The Ascension tab manages various Ascension ability settings including ability restrictions, combo management, and notification options.

docs.title: Etherflash
docs.text: Primarily restricts the teleportation ability. Note that some instances of Etherflash cannot be prevented.

docs.title: Glacial Freeze
docs.text: Prevents ability combos while participating in raid activities.

docs.title: Enable Glacial Freeze Announcing
docs.text:
Primarily for raid scenarios. With higher-tier raid enemies, maintaining Glacial Freeze becomes critical, making fade notifications valuable. This checkbox activates that feature.

Sub-options:

  • Only Announce in raid - Suppresses notifications outside raid groups
  • Announce to OgreIRC instead - Directs notifications to OgreIRC rather than the console
  • Add/text entry - Permits custom duration thresholds
  • Duration to announce listbox - Specifies when notifications trigger (for example: "Glacial Freeze: training dummy -> 44s")

docs.title: Ascension Embargo
docs.text:
Important

Ascension Embargo must be enabled in the Settings tab for these functions to operate.

docs.title: Configuration Options
docs.text: Setting Description Default Ascension Embargo Time Interval between starting ability casts 10 seconds Ascension Delay Time Interval between detecting combos and executing them 1 second Ascension Abilities Master listing of all available ascension abilities -- Ascension To NOT Combo Excludes specified abilities from automatic combos --

docs.title: Assist
docs.text: The Assist tab manages which character your bot will assist during combat.

docs.title: Enable/Disable
docs.text: The Assist functionality is controlled by the Auto Assist checkbox on the Settings tab.

docs.title: Assist Target Dropdown
docs.text: The dropdown menu selects your primary assist target. If the selected person becomes unavailable as an assist target (for example, they are no longer in your raid or group), the system automatically moves to the next person on the list.

docs.title: Usage Notes
docs.text: For real-time assist target changes during gameplay, use OgreMCP's Assist option rather than modifying settings through this tab directly. OgreMCP provides a faster and more convenient way to switch assist targets on the fly.

docs.title: Auto Target
docs.text:
Auto Target provides an automated way to target mobs in a certain order or to target mobs that spawn as part of an encounter.

Important

Auto Target will supersede any auto assist settings when enabled.

docs.title: Core Settings
docs.text:
• Enable Auto Target - Toggles the feature on or off
  • Scan Radius - Determines how far the bot searches for targets
  • Rescan Time - Interval between target searches (in milliseconds)

docs.title: Actor Management
docs.text:
• Actor Name - Any attackable NPC name
  • Reset Actor options - Restores default settings for the selected actor
  • Add Current Target - Adds your current in-game target to the list
  • Min. HP To Target - Health percentage threshold before targeting this actor
  • Actor Order - Prioritization sequence (targets are processed top to bottom)
  • Clear Actors - Empties the entire targeting list

docs.title: List Operations
docs.text:
• Save List as - Saves the current actor list with a custom name
  • Clear - Empties the text box
  • Load selected list - Loads a previously saved configuration
  • Delete selected list - Removes a saved configuration
  • Add Actor - Inserts a new actor from the text box
  • Edit Actor - Modifies the selected actor's properties

docs.title: Key Notes
docs.text:
• Configurations are saved by zone and automatically refreshed upon zoning
  • AutoAssist is disabled when Auto Target is enabled
  • Supports health-based targeting thresholds

Note

This is considered an advanced option and is offered as-is.

docs.title: Cast Stack
docs.text: The Cast Stack tab replaces the previous CA (Casting) system. Abilities execute in top-down order as they become available.

docs.title: Adding Abilities
docs.text: Select an ability from the left list, choose its type, configure options, then click Add Entry. Abilities can be reordered by dragging them in the list.

docs.title: Ability Types
docs.text: Type Description CA Combat Art - no target specification needed NamedCA Named Combat Art - only used against named NPCs NonNamedCA Non-Named Combat Art - only used against non-named mobs Combat Combat ability - target selection required Debuff Debuff ability - toggle debuffing on/off NamedDebuff Named Debuff - only used against named NPCs Heal Heal ability - target and HP percentage threshold required PowerHeal Power Heal ability - target and power percentage threshold required Buff Buff ability - target selection may be required NonCombatBuff Non-Combat Buff - target selection may be required Cure Cure ability - target selection may be required

docs.title: Checkboxes
docs.text: Checkbox Abbreviation Function Ignore Duration [ID] Uses abilities as soon as available, potentially overwriting existing instances Ignore Encounter Nukes [IE] Casts green AE abilities against single mobs Ignore AE Nukes [IAE] Casts blue AE abilities against single mobs Max Increments [MAX] Uses ability only when at maximum increments Named NPCs Only [Named] Restricts casting to Named NPC targets only Requires Item Equipped [RIE] Item must be equipped/worn to activate the ability

docs.title: Numeric Thresholds
docs.text: Setting Description Fervor (</>) Conditional ability firing based on fervor value Dissonance (<=>=) Channeler-specific resource management Savagery Required Beastlord-specific savagery slider threshold My HP (</>) Personal health percentage thresholds My MP (</>) Personal mana/power percentage thresholds NPC HP (</>) Target NPC health percentage thresholds Aggro (</>) Threat level conditions Custom Tag Enable/disable ability groups via MCP button

docs.title: Group Mechanics
docs.text: Heal and Rez abilities use the entered number for targeting decisions (e.g., which group member to heal based on health thresholds).

docs.title: Chat Events
docs.text: The Chat Events tab enables monitoring of chat text for specific phrases and automatic execution of code when triggers occur. This tab must be enabled via the Enable Chat Events checkbox on the Settings 2 tab.

docs.title: Text to watch for
docs.text: The string of text that you want the bot to look for to take action on.

docs.title: Code to execute
docs.text: A single line of code that runs when the monitored text appears. This supports commands from the OgreBotAPI.

docs.title: [OC] On success - Send message to Ogre Console
docs.text: When enabled, the bot will notify you via the Ogre Console upon detecting the watched text.

docs.title: [Ding] On success
docs.text: When enabled, the bot will play an audible sound to notify you of the event when the trigger text is found.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Field Value Text to watch for Hail, Kannkor Code to execute OgreBotAPI:Jump[all] [OC] On success Checked [Ding] On success Checked

Result: The bot monitors chat and, upon detecting "Hail, Kannkor", executes the jump command for all group members while sending a console notification and playing an audio alert.

docs.title: Crowd Control
docs.text: This tab controls all crowd control abilities.

docs.title: Adding abilities to the Cast Order
docs.text: Double-click abilities on the left side to move them to the right (Cast Order) section.

docs.title: Removing abilities from the Cast Order
docs.text: Select an ability by left-clicking, then right-click to remove it.

docs.title: Re-ordering your Cast Order
docs.text: Click and hold an ability within the Cast Order, then drag it up or down to reposition it.

docs.title: Turning abilities On/Off
docs.text:
Double-click abilities in the Cast Order to toggle them:

  • White - Active (will cast)
  • Black - Inactive (will not cast)

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
The crowd control system accepts various crowd control spells including single-target mezes, group mezes, and root abilities.

Key behaviors:

  • Does not affect your assist target or temporary assist targets (like those set via AssistUI)
  • Mezes other hostile creatures that have aggro on you or your group members
  • Re-applies crowd control to targets with less than 10 seconds remaining duration using the same ability
  • Avoids attempting to mez epic-level creatures
  • Will proceed to nuke after mezzing if you lack an assist designation with CAs enabled

docs.title: Debug
docs.text: The Debug tab outputs debug information to the InnerSpace console. It provides four configurable debug options, each controlled by a checkbox.

docs.title: Debug Options
docs.text:
Option Description Casting Debug Displays debug info when the bot casts each spell Casting Details Debug Displays debug info about each spell the bot is trying to cast What is the Bot Doing Displays debug info about the routines the bot is entering and exiting Debugging for Announce Displays debug info about any announces

Each option can be independently enabled or disabled to control which debugging information is output to the InnerSpace console during bot operation.

docs.title: Despawn Events
docs.text: The Despawn Events tab enables monitoring for when certain NPCs despawn and then executes a single line of code when the trigger occurs. This tab must be enabled via the Enable Despawn Events checkbox on the Settings 2 tab.

docs.title: Actor to watch for
docs.text: Specify the NPC name that triggers the bot's monitoring function when it despawns.

docs.title: Code to execute
docs.text: A single line of code to run when the monitored NPC despawns. This accepts commands from the OgreBotAPI.

docs.title: [OC] On success - Send message to Ogre Console
docs.text: When enabled, the bot notifies you via the Ogre Console when the watched NPC despawns.

docs.title: [Ding] On success
docs.text: When enabled, the bot plays an audible sound alert upon detecting the NPC despawning.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Field Value Actor to watch for an iksar child Code to execute OgreBotAPI:Jump[all] [OC] On success Checked [Ding] On success Checked

Result: The bot monitors for "an iksar child" to despawn. Upon detection, it executes OgreBotAPI:Jump[all], causing the entire group to jump. You also receive a console message and audible notification.

docs.title: EQ2 Chars
docs.text: The EQ2 Chars tab is a character management interface for storing and managing your EverQuest 2 character information.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Required Description Character Name Yes The name of the character Account Name No The account associated with the character Password No The account password (for auto-login) Comments No Optional notes about the character

docs.title: Data Storage
docs.text: Character information is stored in /EQ2OgreCommon/DoNotShareWithOthers/EQ2Chars.xml. These settings are saved globally and are not part of your OgreBot profile, allowing a single setup for all characters.

docs.title: Adding and Removing Entries
docs.text:
• Left-click to select an entry
  • Right-click to remove an entry
  • When adding a new entry matching an existing character name, the system removes any entry with the same character name first

docs.title: Editing Behavior
docs.text: When selecting a list item, all fields repopulate except passwords, which remain blank. This protects saved passwords from accidental overwriting during edits.

docs.title: Group/Raid Feature
docs.text: The Add Current Group/Raid button adds all current raid or group members to the character list if they do not already exist.

docs.title: Auto-Login
docs.text:
Using OgreAutoLogin requires all of the following fields to be filled in:

  • Account Name
  • Password
  • Server

docs.title: Display
docs.text: Account name, character name, and server are displayed in the interface. Passwords remain hidden for security.

docs.title: Equipment Info
docs.text:
The Equipment Info tab displays information about the character's currently equipped gear.

Documentation coming soon.

docs.title: HUDs
docs.text:
The HUDs tab provides real-time information displayed on-screen. It replaces the older "Mob/Priest Info" option and allows customization of displayed information, screen position, and update frequency.

Note

Raid/Grind Options currently remain at fixed positions (300,300 to 300,400) and are not yet integrated into this system.

docs.title: Update Interval
docs.text: Measured in frames, this controls the refresh frequency. Higher values improve performance by reducing CPU usage. It is recommended not to go below 5, with 10 being a practical minimum for most users.

docs.title: X Position
docs.text: The horizontal coordinate determining where the HUD displays on screen.

docs.title: Y Position
docs.text: The vertical coordinate for HUD placement. For multi-item displays (group/raid), this marks where the first entry appears.

docs.title: Y Position Increment
docs.text: Applies only to multiple-item displays. Each subsequent entry adds this value to the Y Position, creating vertical spacing between entries.

docs.title: Display nearest NamedNPC/NPC
docs.text: Shows the closest named NPC, or a standard NPC if no named NPC exists nearby.

docs.title: Display nearest PC
docs.text: Identifies the nearest player character outside your group or raid. This option uses significant processing power.

docs.title: Display Group Distance
docs.text:
Lists group members with distance metrics. Color coding indicates proximity:

Color Distance White Less than 30 meters Yellow 30-75 meters Red Greater than 75 meters

docs.title: Display Raid Distance
docs.text:
Shows raid members with distance information. Automatically disables group display when active. Includes spacers every 6 players.

Color Distance White Less than 20 meters Yellow 20-30 meters Orange 30-75 meters Red Greater than 75 meters

docs.title: Raid HUD Example
docs.text: Here is an example of the Raid Distance HUD in action during a raid:

docs.title: Items
docs.text: The Items tab enables you to add clickable items from your inventory to OgreBot's ability rotation system.

docs.title: Refresh Function
docs.text:
The Refresh button loads activatable items from your inventory. This process takes 20-30 seconds because it requires server calls to determine item properties (such as whether they are clickable items).

Warning

DO NOT MODIFY YOUR INVENTORY WHILE THE REFRESH IS RUNNING. Changing your inventory during a refresh can cause array errors that disrupt the scanning operation.

docs.title: Item Management
docs.text:
• Items added to the right side are saved with your profiles
  • All items use the prefix format Item: (for example: Item:Manastone)
  • To remove an item, either delete it from the right side or disable it via double-click
  • Changes take effect only after reloading profiles or restarting the bot

docs.title: Technical Limitations
docs.text:
• No range data exists for items; the default range is set to 30 based on testing
  • No way to verify if items work on group members versus raid members
  • Pet targeting is not supported; items work only on player characters
  • Items cannot be queued like abilities; recovery time detection is unavailable
  • Defensive items forcefully change targets during use

docs.title: Supported Cast Stack Types
docs.text:
Items work with the following cast stack types:

  • Priority-Combat
  • Power Heals
  • CAs
  • NamedCAs
  • Non-combat buffs (defensive items)
  • CA (offensive items)

docs.title: Key Binds
docs.text:
The Key Binds tab allows you to configure keyboard shortcuts for various OgreBot functions.

Documentation coming soon.

docs.title: Load
docs.text: The Load tab determines what settings and actions activate when OgreBot initializes.

docs.title: Radar on
docs.text: Enables radar functionality upon bot startup if this option is selected.

docs.title: Radar off
docs.text: Disables radar when the bot loads, provided radar is currently active.

docs.title: Executes
docs.text: Runs specified script commands and other operations during the bot's initialization sequence. This allows you to automate setup tasks that should occur every time OgreBot loads.

docs.title: Button test
docs.text: Validates user-entered key inputs by displaying confirmation messages in the console window to verify proper functionality.

docs.title: Loot
docs.text:
The Loot tab controls automated responses when loot windows appear in-game.

Note

Leader Only functionality is not available in ISXEQ2. The bot can only read the most recent loot window when multiple appear simultaneously.

docs.title: FFA Loot Options
docs.text:
• Accept any tradable - Automatically accepts tradable items from Free-for-All loot windows
    • Loot everything - Accepts all items including no-trade and heirloom items (requires "Accept any tradable" to be enabled)

docs.title: Lotto Loot Options
docs.text:
• Accept All (including non-tradables) - Automatically clicks the "All" button on lotto loot windows
  • Decline All - Automatically clicks the "Decline" button on lotto loot windows

docs.title: NBG (Need Before Greed) Loot Options
docs.text:
• Need All (including non-tradables) - Automatically selects "Need" on all items
  • Greed All (including non-tradables) - Automatically selects "Greed" on all items
  • Decline All (including non-tradables) - Automatically declines all items

docs.title: Leader Only Loot Options
docs.text:
Warning

Leader Only loot is not available in the current ISXEQ2 implementation.

docs.title: Miscellaneous Options
docs.text:
• Auto Confirm No-Trade and Heirloom - Automatically confirms receipt of no-trade and heirloom restricted items
  • War Rune unpacking - Provides individual and bulk unpack options for War Runes
  • Draconic Phylactery unpacking - Provides individual and bulk unpack options for Draconic Phylacteries
  • Status Bag unpacking - Provides unpack options for status bags
  • Exquisite Chest notification - Plays an audio alert when exquisite chests drop
  • Coin splitting - Distributes currency to group/raid members with a configurable platinum threshold option

docs.title: Usage Notes
docs.text: The Loot tab pairs well with Auto Hunt features. For unattended farming scenarios, it is recommended to set in-game loot to Round-Robin and enable the auto-confirm options.

docs.title: Ogre Console
docs.text: The Ogre Console tab configures the Ogre Console window and IRC settings.

docs.title: Ogre Console Settings
docs.text: Setting Description OgreConsole X Coord Sets the X (horizontal) position of the Ogre Console window OgreConsole Y Coord Sets the Y (vertical) position of the Ogre Console window OgreConsole Width Sets the width of the Ogre Console window OgreConsole Height Sets the height of the Ogre Console window

docs.title: Console Visibility Checkboxes
docs.text: Checkbox Description Show Console on load Opens the console window when the bot loads Hide Console on load Hides the console window when the bot loads Never auto open ogreconsole Prevents the Ogre Console from ever opening automatically (not recommended)

docs.title: IRC Settings
docs.text:
These settings are saved globally (not per-profile).

Setting Description Connect to IRC Automatically connects to IRC on bot load OgreIRC uplink name The name of your PC for IRC identification OgreIRC Server The name of your IRC server OgreIRC User The user name you use in IRC OgreIRC Channel The name of your IRC channel OgreIRC Password The password for your IRC channel

docs.title: On Zone
docs.text: The On Zone tab manages automated actions triggered during zone transitions. It allows you to configure scripts and commands that will automatically run after the player completes a zone change.

docs.title: Executes
docs.text:
The primary feature allows you to configure scripts and commands that will automatically run after completing a zone change. This enables streamlined automation workflows by executing predefined actions upon entering new zones.

Use this to set up actions that should happen every time you zone, such as rebuffing, repositioning, or running initialization scripts.

docs.title: OSA (On Screen Assistant)
docs.text:
The OSA (On Screen Assistant) tab configures the NPC On Screen Assistant feature. This feature must be enabled via the Use NPC On Screen Assistant (OSA) checkbox on the Settings tab.

The OSA provides on-screen tracking and information about NPCs during gameplay.

Documentation coming soon.

docs.title: Other
docs.text: The Other tab contains miscellaneous settings that do not fit into other categories.

docs.title: Cure While Stunned/Stifled
docs.text:
Activates an ability when control effects prevent casting.

Note

This only checks your own status, not the status of others. It may trigger false activations on uncurable debuffs.

docs.title: Resurrect Non-Authorized Group/Raid Members
docs.text: When enabled, allows casting resurrection on any group or raid member, regardless of their authorization list status.

docs.title: Confront Fear Requests
docs.text:
Configure how Confront Fear requests are communicated:

  • Request via Uplink - Sends the request through the Uplink system
  • Request via group chat - Sends the request through group chat
  • Request via raid chat - Sends the request through raid chat

docs.title: Group Cure Management
docs.text:
Not Recommended

Do not cancel group cures when no one has a detrimental - Prevents cancellation of group cures even when no detrimentals are detected.

docs.title: Curse Cure Management
docs.text:
Not Recommended

Do not cancel cure curse when no one has a curse - Prevents cancellation of curse cures even when no curses are detected.

docs.title: Blazing Bow of Light
docs.text: • Use only when needed - Only uses Blazing Bow of Light when the situation requires it

docs.title: Group/Raid Invitations
docs.text:
Not Recommended

Accept Group/Raid Invites from ANYONE nearby - Accepts invites from any nearby player regardless of who they are.

docs.title: Post-Cast
docs.text: The Post-Cast tab is the inverse of the Pre-Cast tab. It will cast a spell after a specified spell is cast.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The configuration works the same as the Pre-Cast tab, but in reverse order -- you specify a trigger spell and an ability to cast after it.

For additional details about the configuration options, refer to the Pre-Cast tab documentation.

docs.title: Pre-Cast
docs.text:
The Pre-Cast tab allows you to configure spells that should cast before other specific spells. This is useful for abilities like Shaman's "Ritual" buff or Sorcerer's "Freehand Sorcery" that need to be active before casting a main spell.

The system checks these conditions whenever the bot attempts to cast a spell.

Note

The spell no longer requires to be maintained. It will be slightly faster (approximately half a second) if it does appear in maintained.

docs.title: Spell to be cast before
docs.text: Designates the spell that executes prior to your main spell (the prerequisite ability).

docs.title: This spell is cast
docs.text: Specifies the actual spell being cast (the primary action).

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: • Double-click an entry to toggle it on or off

docs.title: Example Workflow
docs.text:
You can chain multiple pre-cast spells before a main ability. For instance:

  1. Freehand Sorcery -> Ice Comet
  2. Catalyst -> Ice Comet

If both prerequisites are available, the system executes them sequentially before casting the primary spell (Ice Comet).

docs.title: Relay Groups
docs.text:
The Relay Groups tab manages relay group configurations for inter-session communication.

Documentation coming soon.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: The Settings tab controls high-level on/off functions for the bot. The checkboxes here enable or disable entire categories of behavior. For example, the buff checkbox turns all buffing on or off, while the Buffs tab controls which specific buffs you want.

docs.title: Cast Stack Management
docs.text:
• Disable Cast Stack (CS) - Disables the entire cast stack
  • Disable CS_Buffs - Disables buff casting from the cast stack
  • Disable CS_Cure - Disables cure casting
  • Disable CS_CureCurse - Disables curse curing
  • Disable CS_Heal - Disables healing
  • Disable CS_PowerHeal - Disables power healing
  • Disable CS_Res - Disables resurrection
  • Disable CS_Combat - Disables combat abilities
  • Disable CS_CA - Disables combat arts
  • Disable CS_NamedCA - Disables named-only combat arts
  • Disable CS_NonNamedCA - Disables non-named combat arts
  • Disable CS_Debuff - Disables debuffs
  • Disable CS_NamedDebuff - Disables named-only debuffs
  • Disable CS_Items - Disables item usage

docs.title: Other Functions
docs.text:
• X abilities to group cure - Priests only; cancels current spell to cast group cure
  • Force Named CA - Treats all NPCs as Named
  • Accept Loot - Enables loot acceptance
  • Loot Corpses/Chests - Loots corpses and chests (does not move character)
  • Loot InCombat - Allows looting during combat

docs.title: Column 2 Top: Combat Positioning
docs.text:
• Face mob in combat - Automatically faces the target mob during combat
  • Ranged Attack - Enables ranged auto-attack
  • Melee Attack - Enables melee auto-attack
  • Move into Melee Range - Moves the character into melee range of the target
  • Move Behind Mob - Moves behind the mob (uses collision checks)
  • Move In Front of Mob - Moves in front of the mob (uses collision checks)
  • Turn Off Attack - Disengages auto-attack when target becomes invalid
  • Ignore NPC HP to move - Moves regardless of NPC health percentage
  • Ignore NPC HP (100%) - Ignores NPC HP threshold when at 100%

docs.title: Column 2 Bottom: Items & Nuking
docs.text:
• Enable Consume Items - Enables automatic consumption of items
  • Disable DBC Claim - Disables Daybreak Cash claim functionality
  • Encounter Smart Nukes - Enables smart encounter (green AE) nuke logic
  • AE Smart Nukes - Enables smart AE (blue AE) nuke logic
  • Move to Area/Allow Camp Spot - Enables camp spot movement behavior
  • Auto Assist - Enables automatic assist on the designated target

docs.title: Column 3 Top: Automation Features
docs.text:
• Accept Res - Automatically accepts resurrection
  • Auto Follow Mode - Enables automatic follow behavior
  • Enable Announce Tab - Activates the Announce tab functionality
  • Use NPC On Screen Assistant (OSA) - Enables the On Screen Assistant for NPC tracking
  • Enable OgreMCP - Enables the OgreMCP control panel
  • Enable Aliases - Enables command aliases
  • Auto-Handle HQ Earring - Automatically handles Heritage Quest earring updates
  • Try to keep Familiar up - Automatically resummons familiar if dismissed
  • Do not auto Overseer - Prevents automatic Overseer mission handling
  • Auto Temp Mount Reductions - Automatically applies temporary mount training reductions
  • Auto Temp Research Reductions - Automatically applies temporary research reductions
  • Auto Temp Familiar Experience - Automatically applies temporary familiar experience boosts

docs.title: Column 3 Bottom: Dynamic Settings
docs.text:
• Enable Ability Tracker - Enables ability tracking
  • Dynamic Ignore Encounter Nukes - Dynamically ignores encounter nukes based on conditions
  • Dynamic Ignore PBAE - Dynamically ignores point-blank AE abilities based on conditions
  • Dynamic Camp spot - Dynamically adjusts camp spot behavior
  • Dynamic Assist - Dynamically adjusts assist behavior

docs.title: Raid/Heroic
docs.text:
• Enable Raid Options - Enables raid-specific options
  • Enable Limited Raid Options - Enables a subset of raid options
  • Enable Heroic Setups - Enables heroic dungeon setups
  • Accept Invites - Automatically accepts group/raid invites
  • Accept No Choice Rewards - Automatically accepts rewards with no alternative choices
  • Auto Target when Hated - Automatically targets an NPC when on its hate list
  • Display Mission Info - Displays mission/quest information
  • Auto Share Missions - Automatically shares missions with the group

docs.title: Embargo/Tag Systems
docs.text:
• Enable Ability Embargo - Enables the ability embargo system
  • Enable Tag Embargo - Enables the tag embargo system
  • Enable Tag Allow - Enables the tag allow system
  • Enable Item Embargo - Enables the item embargo system
  • Disable Bulwark of Order - Disables Bulwark of Order usage
  • Disable Auto-Defensives - Disables automatic defensive ability usage
  • Accept Zone-In Confirmation - Automatically accepts zone-in confirmation dialogs

docs.title: Settings 2
docs.text: The Settings 2 tab is an extension of the Settings tab, providing additional on/off toggles for various bot features.

docs.title: Event Controls
docs.text:
• Enable Chat Events - Toggles the Chat Events tab functionality on or off
  • Enable Spawn Events - Activates the Spawn Events tab
  • Enable Despawn Events - Activates the Despawn Events tab

docs.title: Combat & Gameplay
docs.text:
• HO's - Activates the Heroic Opportunity wheel without reordering spells
  • Crowd Control - Enables crowd control mechanics
  • Disable Ability Collision Checks - Allows targeting and casting through obstacles
  • Disable Merc Support - Disables mercenary support
  • Accept Raid Ready Checks - Automatically confirms raid leader readiness checks
  • Accept Dungeon is Ready - Automatically accepts Dungeon Finder group invitations

docs.title: Ability Management
docs.text:
• Disable Pre-Cast Tab - Disables all pre-cast abilities
  • Disable Post-Cast Tab - Disables all post-cast abilities
  • Disable Ogre Fly - Disables Ogre Fly functionality

docs.title: Server & Gameplay Options
docs.text:
• Enable PVP - Allows player combat on PVP servers
  • Do not auto accept quests - Prevents automatic quest acceptance
  • Do not check Research on load - Skips research checks when loading (useful for TLE servers)
  • Do not check Mount Training on load - Skips mount training progress verification on load
  • Skip Cutscenes - Automatically ends cinematics/cutscenes

docs.title: Invisibility Management
docs.text:
• Cancel Invis After Combat - Removes invisibility after combat ends
  • No Invis Casting - Prevents casting while invisible

docs.title: Pet & Interface Options
docs.text:
• Enable Pets in Dropdowns - Shows pet names in selection dropdown menus
  • Do not send pet to attack - Prevents automatic pet engagement

docs.title: Quest & Movement
docs.text:
• Enable Quest Compare - Compares quests across sessions
  • Cast while moving - Allows spell casting during movement

docs.title: Setup
docs.text: The Setup tab manages various miscellaneous options that control bot behavior. Many of these settings require corresponding checkboxes on the Settings tab to be enabled in order to take effect.

docs.title: Combat Engagement Settings
docs.text:
• NPC HP threshold for attacking - Sets the percentage of NPC health at which the bot will begin attacking
  • NPC HP threshold for moving into attack range - Sets the percentage of NPC health at which the bot will move into attack range
  • Pet engagement HP threshold - Sets the NPC health percentage at which pets will engage

docs.title: Resource Management
docs.text:
• Mana requirement percentage to use Combat Arts - Minimum mana percentage required before the bot will use combat arts
  • Health requirement percentage to use Combat Arts - Minimum health percentage required before the bot will use combat arts (helps prevent deaths from health-draining effects)

docs.title: Ability Casting
docs.text:
• Delay time for accepting resurrections - Time delay (measured in tenths of seconds) before accepting a resurrection
  • Target count threshold for Smart AoE abilities (Blue) - Minimum number of targets required before casting blue AE abilities
  • Target count threshold for Smart Encounter abilities (Green) - Minimum number of targets required before casting green encounter abilities
  • Stealth/invisibility ability configuration - Configure stealth or invisibility abilities for classes that require stealth prerequisites

docs.title: Movement & Following
docs.text:
• Maximum melee engagement distance - Maximum distance at which the bot will attempt melee engagement (default: 40)
  • Auto-follow target selection - Select which character to follow
  • Auto-follow activation range - Distance at which auto-follow activates (default: 35)

docs.title: Communication Features
docs.text:
• Broadcast unauthorized private tells through Uplink - Forwards unauthorized tells via the Uplink system
  • Broadcast guild/officer chat through Uplink - Forwards guild and officer chat via the Uplink system
  • Display broadcast messages on-screen - Shows broadcast messages as on-screen notifications
  • Audio notification for incoming broadcast tells - Plays a sound when a broadcast tell is received

docs.title: Spawn Events
docs.text: The Spawn Events tab enables monitoring for specific NPC spawns and executes code when triggers occur. This tab must be enabled via the Enable Spawn Events checkbox on the Settings 2 tab.

docs.title: Actor to watch for
docs.text: Enter the NPC name the bot should detect and respond to when it spawns.

docs.title: Code to execute
docs.text: A single line of code to run when the monitored NPC spawns. This supports basic code and OgreBotAPI commands.

docs.title: [OC] On success - Send message to Ogre Console
docs.text: When enabled, the bot notifies you through the Ogre Console upon detecting the watched NPC spawn.

docs.title: [Ding] On success
docs.text: When enabled, produces an audible alert sound when the target NPC spawns.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Field Value Actor to watch for an iksar child Code to execute OgreBotAPI:Jump[all] [OC] On success Checked [Ding] On success Checked

Result: The bot monitors for "an iksar child" to spawn. Upon detection, it executes OgreBotAPI:Jump[all], causing the entire group to jump. You also receive a console message and audible notification.

docs.title: Unload
docs.text: The Unload tab controls what occurs when OgreBot shuts down.

docs.title: Executes
docs.text: This setting allows you to run scripts and commands during the bot's unload process. Use this to automate cleanup tasks or actions that should occur every time OgreBot is unloaded.

docs.title: Uplink Info
docs.text:
The Uplink Info tab shows the computers you have connected to the Uplink system.

This tab provides a visual overview of all currently connected machines, allowing you to verify that your multi-computer setup is communicating properly.

docs.title: Auto Login
docs.text:
OgreAutoLogin enables opening sessions and logging characters into specific InnerSpace sessions automatically. This is an advanced feature requiring specific setup including Windows shortcuts.

Quick Start

To auto-login a single character, complete the Before You Begin section below, launch EQ2, open the InnerSpace console (~ key), and type ogre login toonname.

docs.title: Before You Begin
docs.text:
Complete all of the following prerequisites before attempting to use Auto Login:

  • A blank loginscene (see the First Run guide)
  • Character login information filled in on the EQ2 Chars tab

  • Computer name(s) configured in the Uplink Info tab
  • ISXOgre set to autoload
  • PC powered on and plugged in
  • InnerSpace running in 64-bit mode (verify via right-click Configuration, confirming Use 64-bit Inner Space Uplink is checked)

docs.title: Step 1: Prerequisites
docs.text: Complete all items in the Before You Begin section. Do not skip any steps.

docs.title: Step 2: Edit AutoLoginSettings.xml
docs.text:
Open the file at:

InnerSpace/Scripts/EQ2OgreCommon/OgreAutoLogin/AutoLoginSettings.xml

Modify these values (case-sensitive):

Setting Value GameName Everquest 2 ProfileName everquest 2 default profile TimeToWaitAfterLoadingASession 150 TimeToWaitBetweenLoadingSessions 50

To find the correct values, right-click the InnerSpace taskbar notification, view the GameName list, and hover over Everquest 2 to see the ProfileName.

docs.title: Step 3: Create a Desktop Shortcut
docs.text:
1. Right-click your desktop and select New > Shortcut
  2. Click Browse and locate InnerSpace.exe
  3. Append runscript eq2ogrecommon/OgreAutoLogin/AutoLogin to the path

Examples:

D:\Games\InnerSpace\InnerSpace.exe runscript eq2ogrecommon/OgreAutoLogin/AutoLogin

"C:\Program Files\Innerspace\InnerSpace.exe" runscript eq2ogrecommon/OgreAutoLogin/AutoLogin

Note

If your path contains spaces, wrap it in quotes.

docs.title: Step 4: Launch the Auto Login UI
docs.text:
Double-click the desktop shortcut. The UI loads inside the Uplink console and may appear in the background or as a taskbar window.

If the window is missing, right-click the InnerSpace icon and select Console.

docs.title: Step 5: Configure Character Login Profiles
docs.text:
Setting up the character list:

  1. Select the first character from the Character List
  2. Select the PC for this character
  3. Select the InnerSpace Session name (e.g., IS1)
  4. Click Add Selection
  5. Repeat for each character

Session behavior:

Session Behavior Any Character stays on its current session Specific (IS1, IS2, etc.) If the character is online, it verifies the correct session. If offline, it logs off that session if in use

Warning

Alt characters currently logged on will be disconnected to allow the selected characters to log in.

Saving profiles:

  1. Type a profile name on the right side
  2. Click Save Profile
  3. Saved profiles appear under Load Profile next time
  4. Click Load Toons and exit
  5. Wait for all characters to log in (this can take several minutes)
  6. Close the InnerSpace Console

docs.title: Step 6: Repeat
docs.text: Launch the shortcut any time you need to log your characters in.

docs.title: Loading a Specific Profile Automatically
docs.text:
Once you have saved a profile through the UI, you can create a shortcut that bypasses the UI entirely:

  1. Create a new Desktop Shortcut (same method as above)
  2. Append the profile name to the path:
D:\Games\InnerSpace\InnerSpace.exe runscript eq2ogrecommon/OgreAutoLogin/AutoLogin MainGroup

Replace MainGroup with your saved profile name. This shortcut will automatically log your characters without showing the UI.

docs.title: Using Multiple Computers
docs.text: All computers must be connected before running AutoLogin shortcuts.

docs.title: Create a Connection Shortcut
docs.text:
1. Create a shortcut to InnerSpace.exe
  2. Append: runscript eq2ogrecommon/ogreconnect
D:\Games\InnerSpace\InnerSpace.exe runscript eq2ogrecommon/ogreconnect

Name it Ogre Connect. Nothing visible happens when you run it -- it simply connects the computers. All computers must use identical naming in InnerSpace game profile configuration.

docs.title: Multi-Computer Startup Sequence
docs.text:
1. Launch InnerSpace on all computers
  2. Double-click the Ogre Connect shortcut
  3. Double-click the Auto Login shortcut (UI or specific profile)

docs.title: Quirks and Known Issues
docs.text:
• Start InnerSpace before double-clicking shortcuts. Launching InnerSpace from shortcuts may skip parameters if patching is needed.
  • There is limited user error checking -- use common sense with character/session assignments.
  • Occasional session crashes when rearranging characters (rare, not reproducible). If a crash occurs, check the Uplink console for the line Command given: ogre -<stuff>- and report the <stuff> portion.
  • Loading Ogre AutoLogin loads ISXOgre into Uplink. If you need to patch ISXOgre while in-game, unload it via console: ext -unload isxogre

docs.title: Collection Manager
docs.text: The Ogre Collection Manager automatically scribes collectibles from your collection depots or inventory.

docs.title: Depot Version
docs.text:
Stand near a collection depot and run one of the following commands:

ogre collection
ogre collections
ogre cm

The script navigates through the collection depot inventory and adds every collectible to your collections. It works with both standard and large collection depots, automatically selecting the closest one.

Optional parameters:

Command Description ogre cm -large Force use of the large depot ogre cm -small Force use of the small depot

To stop:

ogre end collection
ogre end collections
ogre end cm

docs.title: Inventory Version
docs.text:
To scribe collectibles directly from your inventory:

ogre cm 1
ogre cm -inventory

The script goes through your inventory and adds every collectible to your collections.

To stop: Same end commands as the depot version.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Only requirement is proximity to a collection depot (for depot version)
  • On completion, you will see a summary message, e.g.: Ogre Collection Manager added 125 collectibles in 407.1 Seconds.

docs.title: Harvesting
docs.text:
Ogre Harvest automates resource gathering in EverQuest 2. It uses OgreMapper waypoints to navigate a zone and harvest nodes along the way.

Requirements

OgreBot must be running before you start Ogre Harvest. You must also have a mapped path for the zone you want to harvest in (see OgreMapper).

docs.title: Step 1: Map Your Zone
docs.text:
Use OgreMapper to create waypoints in the zone you want to harvest. When mapping for harvesting:

  • Name custom points roughly every 40 meters or at logical locations
  • Navigate around obstacles extensively to create navigational points
  • For loop paths, position the final point near the starting point

docs.title: Step 2: Launch
docs.text:
Open the tool using the console command:

Ogre Harvest

docs.title: Step 3: Configure Your Path
docs.text:
1. Click Refresh to load your Nav Paths list
  2. Add each waypoint sequentially to the path list
  3. For non-loop paths, add the points in reverse order at the end to create a return route
  4. Save the path for future reuse

docs.title: Step 4: Select Harvest Types
docs.text: Choose which types of harvest nodes you want to collect (ore, wood, roots, etc.).

docs.title: Step 5: Configure Path Mode
docs.text: Set whether the path runs continuously in a loop or executes once.

docs.title: Step 6: Configure Roam Mode
docs.text: Determine whether movement away from the established path is permitted and set the maximum roaming distance.

docs.title: Step 7: Tether Mode
docs.text: Tether mode is an advanced option. Consult the developer if you need to use it.

docs.title: Step 8: Start Harvesting
docs.text: Click Start to begin the harvest run.

docs.title: Statistics
docs.text: Monitor the statistics window during operation to track harvest counts and progress.

docs.title: Inventory Manager
docs.text:
The Ogre Inventory Manager provides comprehensive inventory automation for selling, trading, brokering, destroying, transmuting, depot management, restocking, quiver refilling, and crafting material management.

To open the Inventory Manager, type in the console:

ogre im

Use At Your Own Risk

The Inventory Manager is powerful and can sell, destroy, or trade items automatically. The developer is not responsible for any lost, sold, or destroyed items.

docs.title: Tabs
docs.text:
The Inventory Manager contains nine functional tabs:

Tab Purpose Sell Sell items to merchants Trade Trade items between characters Broker List items on the broker Destroy Destroy items from inventory T.S.E Transmute, Salvage, or Extract items Depot Deposit items into depots Restock Pull items from containers Quiver Refill ammunition Crafting Mats Pull crafting materials from depots

docs.title: Sell
docs.text: Sells all items from a list you create to a merchant.

docs.title: How to Use
docs.text:
1. Open a merchant window in-game
  2. The Merchant List shows available items. Items already in your saved list appear in green.
  3. Double-click an item to add it to the Saved List (auto-saves to XML)
  4. Right-click an item in the Saved List to remove it
  5. Click Start Selling to begin

docs.title: CLI Commands
docs.text:
ogre im -sell -end
Flag Description -sell Start the sell process -end / -endwhenfinished End the script after processing completes

docs.title: API Methods
docs.text: Method Description OgreIMAPI.Sell:Start Start selling OgreIMAPI.Sell:Add_To_List["Item Name","-save"] Add item to list OgreIMAPI.Sell:Remove_From_List["Item Name","-save"] Remove item from list OgreIMAPI.Sell:Clear_List["-save"] Clear entire saved list

docs.title: Trade
docs.text: Trades items from character to character. Can trade to multiple people in one use.

docs.title: How to Use
docs.text:
1. Select items from the Inventory List
  2. Enter the target character name in Trade To (or use the auto-target button)
  3. Set the Quantity to Trade (use 0 for all of that item)
  4. Optionally enable Partial Item Name matching
  5. Click Add Item to build the final list
  6. Right-click items in the Final List to remove them
  7. Click Start Trading to begin

Note

The inventory list does not filter untradeable items to avoid 3-5 minute server delays.

docs.title: Broker
docs.text: Lists items on the broker automatically.

docs.title: How to Use
docs.text:
1. Select which Broker Bags to scan using the checkboxes
  2. Optionally enable Price Match to match the lowest broker price
  3. Choose a listing mode:
    • List all items from selected bags
    • Un-Listed only -- only items not currently listed
    • Selected only -- only highlighted items (use ++ctrl+left-button++ for multiple selections)
  4. Choose a pricing mode:
    • Skip item prices -- bypass price configuration
    • Set missing prices -- configure prices for items without one
    • Force set prices -- configure prices for all items

docs.title: Set Prices Window
docs.text: Field Description Minimum Price Lowest acceptable listing price. Items below this will not list. Default Price Used when no broker listings exist for the item Static Price Overrides all other pricing, forcing a fixed price

docs.title: Broker Listing Colors
docs.text: Color Meaning Green Listed successfully Red Existing listings undercut your minimum price Purple Item not on broker and no default price set

docs.title: Destroy
docs.text: Destroys items from your inventory based on a saved list. It destroys all of an item if it exists in your inventory.

docs.title: How to Use
docs.text:
1. The Inventory List shows all items. Items already in your saved list appear in green.
  2. Double-click an item to add it to the destruction list (auto-saves)
  3. Right-click an item in the Saved List to remove it
  4. Select which bags to process using the checkboxes
  5. Click Start Destroying to begin

docs.title: CLI Commands
docs.text: ogre im -destroy -end

docs.title: API Methods
docs.text: Method Description OgreIMAPI.Destroy:Start Start destroying OgreIMAPI.Destroy:Add_To_List["Item Name","-save"] Add item OgreIMAPI.Destroy:Remove_From_List["Item Name","-save"] Remove item OgreIMAPI.Destroy:Set_Settings["-bag",2,TRUE] Configure bag settings OgreIMAPI.Destroy:Clear_List["-save"] Clear entire list

docs.title: T.S.E (Transmute, Salvage, Extract)
docs.text: Processes items using Transmute, Salvage, or Extract based on your selections.

docs.title: How to Use
docs.text:
1. Select the desired commands (Salvage and Transmute cannot run simultaneously)
  2. Select which bags to process
  3. Select item tiers to include
  4. Set level range (minimum and maximum)
  5. Optionally set a Resolve Range -- processes items with resolve at or under the entered amount
  6. Click Start TSE

docs.title: CLI Commands
docs.text:
ogre im -tse -end

Alternate flag: -t.s.e

docs.title: API Methods
docs.text:
Method Description OgreIMAPI.TSE:Start Start TSE OgreIMAPI.TSE:Set_Settings["-transmute",TRUE] Enable transmute OgreIMAPI.TSE:Set_Settings["-salvage",TRUE] Enable salvage OgreIMAPI.TSE:Set_Settings["-extract",TRUE] Enable extract

Additional Set_Settings parameters: -treasured, -legendary, -mastercrafted, -fabled, -masters, -mythical, -celestial, -enableresolve, -bag <num> <TRUE/FALSE>, -min <level>, -max <level>, -resolve <level>

docs.title: Depot
docs.text: Deposits items from your inventory into depots based on your selections.

docs.title: How to Use
docs.text:
1. Select Depot Size: Small, Large, or Nearest
  2. Check the Depots you want to use (shown in purple)
  3. Check Depot Options for each depot (shown in orange). Selecting "All" disables other options.
  4. Or check All of the Above to select everything
  5. Click Start Depot

docs.title: CLI Commands
docs.text: ogre im -depot -end

docs.title: API Methods
docs.text:
Method Description OgreIMAPI.Depot:Start Start depot process OgreIMAPI.Depot:Set_Settings["-harvestdepot",TRUE] Enable harvest depot

Available depot parameters: -nearestdepot, -smalldepot, -largedepot, -harvestdepot, -spelldepot, -collectibledepot, -faddepot, -consumabledepot, -laldepot, -adorndepot, -fueldepot, -ammodepot, -alldepot

Each depot has sub-options (e.g., -harvestall, -harvestcommon, -harvesttreasured, -harvestlegendary, -harvestfabled, -harvestrare).

docs.title: Restock
docs.text: Pulls items from containers (consumable, adornment, food & drink depots) based on a saved list.

docs.title: How to Use
docs.text:
1. Click Refresh List to scan available depots
  2. Highlight items from the Depot List, set the Quantity to Restock, and click Add Item
  3. Or use Manual Item Entry to type item names (use the Examine button to pull names from examine windows)
  4. Build your list, then Save List As with a name (minimum 4 characters)
  5. Use Load List to reload saved lists
  6. Click Start Restock to begin

docs.title: CLI Commands
docs.text: ogre im -restock -end

docs.title: API Methods
docs.text: Method Description OgreIMAPI.Restock:Start Start restocking OgreIMAPI.Restock:Load_List["List Name"] Load a saved list OgreIMAPI.Restock:Add_Item["Item Name",Qty] Add item with quantity

docs.title: Quiver
docs.text: Automatically refills ammunition. Prioritizes ammo already in your ammo bag, then draws from a default or custom list if the bag is empty.

docs.title: How to Use
docs.text:
1. Click Refresh List to scan ammo depots
  2. Select items and check the Type of Ammo (arrow, bolt, or throwing)
  3. Click Add Item (at least one ammo type must be checked, no duplicate types allowed)
  4. Save your list and click Start Quiver

docs.title: CLI Commands
docs.text: ogre im -quiver -end

docs.title: API Methods
docs.text: Method Description OgreIMAPI.Quiver:Start Start quiver process OgreIMAPI.Quiver:Load_List["List Name"] Load a saved list

docs.title: Crafting Mats
docs.text: Pulls crafting materials from Harvest depots, Fuel depots, and Fuel Merchants based on a saved list.

docs.title: How to Use
docs.text:
1. Click Refresh List to scan harvest/fuel depots and fuel merchants
  2. Highlight items, set the Quantity, and click Add Item
  3. Or use Manual Item Entry with the Examine button
  4. Save your list and click Start Craft Mats

docs.title: CLI Commands
docs.text: ogre im -craftmats -end

docs.title: API Methods
docs.text: Method Description OgreIMAPI.CraftMats:Start Start craft mats process OgreIMAPI.CraftMats:Load_List["List Name"] Load a saved list OgreIMAPI.CraftMats:Add_Item["Item Name",Qty] Add item with quantity

docs.title: General CLI Notes
docs.text:
All tab commands can be chained together:

ogre im -sell -depot -tse -end

The -end or -endwhenfinished flag should always be passed last. It terminates the Inventory Manager script after all processing completes.

docs.title: IRC Remote Commands (AutoLogin / Session Management)
docs.text:
Added: 2026-04-19

Untested

These commands have been written but not yet tested live. Treat this as a reference-in-progress. If you try them and something misbehaves, report back and the docs will be updated.

docs.title: What This Is
docs.text:
Five new IRC commands let you drive AutoLogin and session management on a remote computer from your IRC client. You send !c <targetclient> -<switch> <args> in the shared IRC channel; the target machine runs the action locally and echoes replies back to the channel.

They run once at the uplink level on the target machine (same dispatch point as -auth / -authlist), not per-session. This is intentional — opening a new session or killing an existing one is an uplink-scope action, not something every session should re-parse.

Auth: each command checks that the sender is on the target's auth list before running. If you aren't authed, the command is silently ignored.

docs.title: The Commands
docs.text:
Switch Purpose -List_AutoLoginProfiles [-profile <name>] [-details] Read and list AutoLogin profiles configured on the target machine. -List_Sessions One-line list of all InnerSpace sessions on the target machine, with PIDs. -LaunchAutoLogin <profile> Run a named AutoLogin profile locally. -OSExecute <command line...> Run an arbitrary OS command. -KillSession <name\|all> Kill one named InnerSpace session, or all sessions except the uplink. -LoadCharacter <toon>[:<session>] Log a character into an existing session, or open a new one.
